senses.gloss: ? mūdhāma (m.; so text by em.; read rather mudhāma or mūḍhāma), acc. to context apparently idle or deluded religious longings, see s.v. 2 āma: ŚsP 〔485.(14—)15〕 (na ca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo) mūdhāmaṃ patati, text. But this is an em.; all mss. mūrdhānaṃ, and so in same locution 17, where ed. inconsistently reads with mss. Note to 15 suggests reading mudhāmaṃ and interprets by [] vyartha-dharmābhilāṣaḥ. The ŚsP itself authorizes this interpretation of āma. It gives no hint as to how it read or interpreted the prior member; it might be Skt. and Pali mudhā, as ed. suggests, or mūḍha, deluded. It seems clear from the context that the mss. reading is corrupt and that the true text had a cpd. ending -āmaṃ (acc. sg.).

mudhāya, seems to be a quasi-instr. sg. fem. to Skt. and Pali (adv.) mudhā (= Pkt. muhāi, Sheth s.v. muhā), in vain: na mudhāya bhavān samudgato LV 〔364.22〕 (vs). Alternatively, ya could perhaps be taken as rel. pron.(= yaḥ), but this seems forced.
